message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"06b5d3fe788760b5cb896e8fed6cd5bd29f2a4348bf798263670fe107580a3f9","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-tn-class-d:lineage:102","source_registry_sha256":"8b0b6a068a0aa720d419171b5007a2610ed6c5012eeff522b57713cf9226eb71","units":[{"unit_id":"sec02-u01","module_id":"sec02-m01","objective_ids":["sec02-u01"],"title":{"text":"Documents that prove identity","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R01","sec02-R07"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Every application depends on documents the Department will accept, and the wrong kind of copy is turned away.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R07"]},{"text":"Original applicants and renewals follow different identity rules.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Tom is applying for his first Tennessee license and brings a union card and a work ID.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-R02"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Both are Secondary items, and an original applicant needs at least one item from the Primary list.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F12"]},"result":{"text":"Tom must swap one of them for a Primary item, such as a certified birth certificate or a valid passport.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-R02"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking any two identity items work for a first license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12"]},"correction":{"text":"Any two items from either list work only for duplicates and renewals; an original applicant needs at least one Primary item.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"First license: one Primary at least; renewal: any two.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"A first-time applicant brings a work ID and a check stub. Will the examiner accept them as the two identity items?","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-R02"]},"answer":{"text":"No. Both are Secondary items, and an original applicant needs at least one Primary item.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-R02"]},"rationale":{"text":"The Primary list holds the core documents, and the second item may come from either list.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-F12"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Proving who you are","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F01","sec02-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Originals or certified copies only.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F01","sec02-R07"]},{"text":"Every document can be verified.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F01","sec02-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Applying for a Tennessee license starts with paperwork, and this lesson shows which documents prove who you are. The Department asks every applicant to prove full legal name and date of birth so it can confirm identity and reduce fraud. Every document on the application checklist must be an original or a certified copy, and faxes and photocopies are turned away. Every document is also subject to verification with the agency that issued it, and that verification can delay issuance of a permit, license or ID. So bring the right originals and allow time for checks.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F01","sec02-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Primary and Secondary lists","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-R03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Primary: birth certificate, passport, military ID, out-of-state photo license.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-R03"]},{"text":"Secondary: check stubs, union cards, work IDs, tax forms.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-R03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Identity documents fall into two lists. Primary identification includes items such as a certified birth certificate, a valid passport, a military ID or a photo license from another state. Secondary identification covers supporting items such as check stubs, union cards, work IDs and tax forms. A computerized check stub counts as secondary identification only when the applicant's full name is pre-printed on it. Think of the Primary list as the core documents and the Secondary list as supporting documents that back them up.","fact_ids":["sec02-R02","sec02-R03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":33,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"How many items you need","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F06"]},"lines":[{"text":"Original applicants: two items, at least one Primary.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F06"]},{"text":"Duplicates and renewals: any two from either list.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F06"]},{"text":"New residents hand in the former license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F06"]}],"narration":{"text":"The examiner asks for two identity items. An original applicant must supply at least one from the Primary list, with the second from either list. Applicants for a duplicate or renewal of an existing Tennessee license or ID may supply any two identity items from either list. New residents must hand in the license from their former state, and if it was lost, they provide the same two identity items as an original applicant. A new resident's valid license from the former state can prove identity, but it never proves US citizenship or lawful permanent residency.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F06"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Documents that get refused","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Hospital and baptismal certificates refused.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R04"]},{"text":"Expired passports refused.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R04"]},{"text":"Replica Social Security cards refused.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Several look-alike documents are refused. A birth certificate must be certified, sealed and issued by an authorized agency such as the Bureau of Vital Statistics, and hospital-issued or baptismal certificates are refused. An expired passport is not accepted, and a passport, birth certificate or license not written in English must come with a Certificate of Accurate Translation. A Social Security card used as identification must be the original, never a metal or plastic replica. Check each document against these rules before your visit so it is not turned away at the counter.","fact_ids":["sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Why originals matter","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R07"]},"lines":[{"text":"Faxes and photocopies are turned away.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R07"]},{"text":"Verification can delay issuance.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R07"]}],"narration":{"text":"It helps to see why the original rule appears again and again. Every document on the checklist must be an original or a certified copy, so faxes and photocopies are turned away at the start. Even accepted documents are subject to verification with the agency that issued them, and that verification can delay issuance of a permit, license or ID. Put together, those two rules mean the safest plan is simple: bring originals or certified copies of every item on the checklist, and expect that the Department may still check them with the agencies that issued them.","fact_ids":["sec02-F01","sec02-R07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Identity items check","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-R02","sec02-R03","sec02-F13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Do a work ID and a check stub satisfy a first-time applicant?","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-R02","sec02-R03","sec02-F13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: a first-time applicant brings a work ID and a computerized check stub with the full name pre-printed, and offers them as the two identity items. Will the examiner accept them? Work it out before reading on. No. Both items are on the Secondary list, and an original applicant must supply at least one item from the Primary list, with the second from either list. A certified birth certificate, a valid passport, a military ID or a photo license from another state would fix the problem. A renewal applicant, by contrast, could use any two items.","fact_ids":["sec02-F12","sec02-R02","sec02-R03","sec02-F13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Identity in one view","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F01","sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two items; one Primary for first licenses.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F01","sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R04"]},{"text":"Originals, translations and no replicas.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F01","sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"To wrap up, every applicant proves full legal name and date of birth. Original applicants bring two identity items with at least one from the Primary list, while renewals may use any two from either list, and new residents surrender their former license. Bring originals or certified copies, never faxes or photocopies. Birth certificates must be certified and sealed by an authorized agency, passports must be current, documents not in English need a Certificate of Accurate Translation, and a Social Security card must be the original. Next, we look at proving citizenship or legal presence.","fact_ids":["sec02-R01","sec02-F12","sec02-F13","sec02-F14","sec02-F01","sec02-F15","sec02-F16","sec02-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u02","module_id":"sec02-m02","objective_ids":["sec02-u02"],"title":{"text":"Citizenship and legal presence","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F11","sec02-R13"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Many applicants must prove US citizenship or lawful permanent residency, not only first-timers.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-R13"]},{"text":"Applicants with temporary legal presence have their own path to a license.","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Grace was first licensed in Tennessee in two thousand ten and is renewing for the first time.","fact_ids":["sec02-R13"]},"reasoning":{"text":"Anyone first issued a Tennessee license after the start of two thousand one must show citizenship or permanent-residency documents at the first renewal and cannot renew that time by mail or online.","fact_ids":["sec02-R13","sec02-F08"]},"result":{"text":"Grace renews in person and brings her citizenship documents.","fact_ids":["sec02-R13"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a temporary resident can get a regular license by passing the tests.","fact_ids":["sec02-F09"]},"correction":{"text":"An applicant with only temporary legal presence cannot get a regular license or ID, but may qualify for a TDL or TID by proving authorized stay.","fact_ids":["sec02-F09"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Prove status at the start, the return and the first renewal.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-R13"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Must a TDL applicant still meet Tennessee's examination requirements?","fact_ids":["sec02-F10"]},"answer":{"text":"Yes. A TDL or TID applicant must meet every examination requirement for driving Class XD or Class XM vehicles.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10"]},"rationale":{"text":"The temporary license changes the credential, not the testing standard.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F09"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Proving your status","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Citizenship or permanent residency.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},{"text":"Temporary legal presence has its own path.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers who must prove US citizenship or lawful permanent residency, which documents prove it, and what applicants with temporary legal presence can receive. Proof is required of first-time applicants, new and returning residents, anyone reinstating after a revocation, suspension or cancellation, and anyone licensed since the start of two thousand one who is renewing for the first time. An applicant who has only temporary legal presence follows a different path, which leads to a temporary credential rather than a regular license or ID.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Accepted proofs","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Certified US birth certificate.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"Valid US passport.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"Certificate of Citizenship or Naturalization.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"Permanent Resident card.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Accepted proof of citizenship or permanent residency includes a certified birth certificate from a US state or territory, a valid US passport, a Certificate of Citizenship or Naturalization, and a Permanent Resident card. Notice that a valid license from another state is not on this list. It can prove identity, but it never proves US citizenship or lawful permanent residency. So a new resident who brings only an out-of-state license still needs one of these documents to show status, even though the old license helps with identity.","fact_ids":["sec02-F11","sec02-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The first renewal","fact_ids":["sec02-R13","sec02-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"First licensed after two thousand one?","fact_ids":["sec02-R13","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"Show documents at the first renewal.","fact_ids":["sec02-R13","sec02-F08"]},{"text":"No mail or online renewal that time.","fact_ids":["sec02-R13","sec02-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Status proof is not only for first licenses. Anyone first issued a Tennessee license or photo ID after the start of two thousand one must show citizenship or permanent-residency documents at the first renewal, and cannot renew that time by mail or online. This matches the broader rule that anyone licensed since the start of two thousand one who is renewing for the first time must prove status. After that first in-person renewal, the documents are on record. Plan for this visit when your first renewal comes due. That is the key point to remember about the first renewal.","fact_ids":["sec02-R13","sec02-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Temporary, not regular","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Temporary presence: no regular license or ID.","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},{"text":"TDL or TID by proving authorized stay.","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},{"text":"Same exams for Class XD or XM.","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"A common misunderstanding is that a temporary resident who passes the tests can receive a regular license. That is not the rule. An applicant who has only temporary legal presence cannot get a regular license or ID, but may qualify for a Temporary Driver License or Temporary Identification License by proving authorized stay. The tests do not get easier either. A TDL or TID applicant must still meet every Tennessee examination requirement for driving Class XD or Class XM vehicles. The temporary path changes the credential, not the standard.","fact_ids":["sec02-F09","sec02-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Temporary license check","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Does a TDL applicant skip any exams?","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F09"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: an applicant with temporary legal presence asks whether a Temporary Driver License comes with lighter testing than a regular license. What is the answer? Work it out before reading on. The answer is no. A TDL or TID applicant must still meet every Tennessee examination requirement for driving Class XD or Class XM vehicles. The difference is in the credential and how long it lasts, not in the tests. The applicant also proves authorized stay, which is what makes the temporary credential possible in the first place.","fact_ids":["sec02-F10","sec02-F09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u02-s6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Status recap","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-R13","sec02-F11","sec02-F09","sec02-F25"]},"lines":[{"text":"Many applicants must prove status.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-R13","sec02-F11","sec02-F09","sec02-F25"]},{"text":"Temporary licenses last for the stay, up to five years.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-R13","sec02-F11","sec02-F09","sec02-F25"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, proof of citizenship or permanent residency is required of first-time applicants, new and returning residents, reinstating drivers, and first-time renewers licensed since the start of two thousand one, who must renew that first time in person. Accepted proofs include a certified US birth certificate, a valid US passport and the citizenship and residency certificates. Applicants with temporary legal presence may get a TDL or TID, which lasts for the authorized stay and costs a flat twenty-eight dollars, up to the maximum of five years.","fact_ids":["sec02-F08","sec02-R13","sec02-F11","sec02-F09","sec02-F25"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec02-u03","module_id":"sec02-m03","objective_ids":["sec02-u03"],"title":{"text":"Residency and Social Security","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F17","sec02-F18"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Residency proofs must be current and show a real street address.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02"]},{"text":"Your Social Security number is required whenever one has been issued, and it is protected on your record.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Mia brings a bank check and an insurance wallet card as her two residency proofs.","fact_ids":["sec02-F18"]},"reasoning":{"text":"A utility initial deposit receipt, bank checks and insurance wallet cards do not count as proof of residency.","fact_ids":["sec02-F18"]},"result":{"text":"Mia must bring two accepted proofs instead, such as a bank statement and a signed lease, each dated within four months.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F02"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking a former Tennessee license means returning residents can skip residency proof.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19"]},"correction":{"text":"Residency proof is demanded from returning residents too, even if they once held a Tennessee license before moving away.","fact_ids":["sec02-F19"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Two proofs, street address, four months fresh.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"Which of these is not a residency proof: a bank statement, a signed lease, or an insurance wallet card?","fact_ids":["sec02-F18","sec02-F17"]},"answer":{"text":"The insurance wallet card does not count.","fact_ids":["sec02-F18"]},"rationale":{"text":"Bank statements and signed leases are accepted, while wallet cards, bank checks and deposit receipts are not.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F18"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Showing where you live","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F19"]},"lines":[{"text":"Two current residency proofs.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F19"]},{"text":"Social Security number rules.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F19"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers proof of Tennessee residency and the rules for Social Security numbers. Applicants bring two proofs of Tennessee residency showing their name and street address, with no post office boxes, and each must be current, meaning dated within the last four months. Residency proof is demanded from first-time, new-resident and returning-resident applicants for every ID, TDL, permit and license class, even if they once held a Tennessee license before moving away. Then we turn to the Social Security number on your application.","fact_ids":["sec02-F02","sec02-F19"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":34,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Accepted residency proofs","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F20"]},"lines":[{"text":"Utility bill with postmarked envelope.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F20"]},{"text":"Bank statement, lease or mortgage, insurance policy.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F20"]},{"text":"Vehicle or voter registration, W-two, tax receipt.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F20"]}],"narration":{"text":"Acceptable residency proofs include a current utility bill with its postmarked envelope, a bank statement, a signed lease or mortgage, an insurance policy, Tennessee vehicle or voter registration, a W-two, or a property tax receipt from within the last year. Residency documents may name the applicant, the applicant's spouse, or for a minor a parent or legal guardian, and the relationship is then shown with a certified marriage certificate or long-form birth certificate. So a married applicant may use a bill in a spouse's name with the marriage certificate.","fact_ids":["sec02-F17","sec02-F20"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s3","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Proofs that do not count","fact_ids":["sec02-F18","sec02-F17"]},"lines":[{"text":"Utility initial deposit receipts.","fact_ids":["sec02-F18","sec02-F17"]},{"text":"Bank checks.","fact_ids":["sec02-F18","sec02-F17"]},{"text":"Insurance wallet cards.","fact_ids":["sec02-F18","sec02-F17"]}],"narration":{"text":"Some papers look like residency proof but do not count. A utility initial deposit receipt, bank checks and insurance wallet cards do not count as proof of residency. Compare them carefully with the accepted list. A current utility bill with its postmarked envelope counts, but the deposit receipt from opening the account does not. A bank statement counts, but a bank check does not. An insurance policy counts, but the small insurance card from your wallet does not. When in doubt, choose the full statement or policy rather than the slip or card.","fact_ids":["sec02-F18","sec02-F17"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Your Social Security number","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-F22","sec02-R08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Required whenever one was issued.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-F22","sec02-R08"]},{"text":"Kept on record, never printed.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-F22","sec02-R08"]},{"text":"Mismatch means more proof.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-F22","sec02-R08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Tennessee law requires your Social Security number on the application whenever the US Government has issued you one, and the number is kept on your record but never printed on the license. If the number does not match federal records, the examiner asks for more proof and may send you to the Social Security Administration before accepting the application. A Social Security number can be proven with an original card, a W-two showing the full number, an employer payroll stub or bank statement with the number, or a health insurance card showing name and number.","fact_ids":["sec02-F21","sec02-F22","sec02-R08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Never issued a number","fact_ids":["sec02-F23"]},"lines":[{"text":"Sign a sworn affidavit in person.","fact_ids":["sec02-F23"]},{"text":"Before an examiner or notary.","fact_ids":["sec02-F23"]},{"text":"Sign a new one each time.","fact_ids":["sec02-F23"]}],"narration":{"text":"Someone who was never issued a Social Security number must sign a sworn affidavit in person before an examiner or notary, under penalty of perjury. That affidavit is not a one-time step. The applicant must sign a new one with every later application. So the affidavit replaces the number on each application, and it must be signed in person each time. Keep this in mind when helping a family member who has never had a number, because the visit to an examiner or notary will repeat with every application they make. The affidavit must be signed again every time.","fact_ids":["sec02-F23"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec02-u03-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Residency proof check","fact_ids":["sec02-F18","sec02-F17","sec02-F02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Which item is not a residency proof?","fact_ids":["sec02-F18","sec02-F17","sec02-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: an applicant lays out three papers, a bank statement, a signed lease and an insurance wallet card, and asks which ones count as proof of Tennessee residency. Work it out before reading on. The bank statement and the signed lease are accepted proofs. The insurance wallet card does not count, along with bank checks and utility initial deposit receipts.
